name: dooinney-oie (night-man)

attributes.attribute: kindly disposed to sailors and farmers
warned of storms by calling, howling, or sounding a horn

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The dooinney-oie is a Manx folkloric figure. The name means "night-man." He was a kindly water spirit. He warned sailors and farmers of storms. He warned them by calling, howling, or sounding a horn.

okr.objective: Records the dooinney-oie, a kindly Manx water spirit who warned people of storms.
key_results: The dooinney-oie is a Manx folkloric figure whose name means 'night-man.'
He was a kindly water spirit.
He warned sailors and farmers of coming storms.
He warned by calling, howling, or sounding a horn.
